headline: Stolen-wallet task is solvable, but it records the freeze-then-unfreeze history and leans on reading a pending refund as a refund rather than a pending transaction.

issues.summary: Same as task_078: the gold freezes all three cards, then unfreezes all three to close them, and the freeze/unfreeze dates persist on the closed cards. Closing the confirmed-stolen cards directly gives the same outcome but a different debit_cards table.
evidence: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026: "If customer confirms the card is lost/stolen, recommend closing instead of freezing"
doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026: "CLOSE: Permanent deactivation - cannot be reversed. Use when card is confirmed lost/stolen"
tools.py close_debit_card_4721: "Only ACTIVE or PENDING cards can be closed." (a FROZEN card must be unfrozen first)
freeze_debit_card_3892 writes card["frozen_date"]; unfreeze_debit_card_3893 writes card["unfrozen_date"]; both fields stay on the closed card in the gold DB
gold[4..6] freeze ev/lb/green; gold[13..15] unfreeze ev/lb/green; gold[17..19] close reason "stolen"
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that follows doc_026 for a confirmed theft fails, even though every card ends CLOSED as in the gold.
issues.suggested_fix: Do not persist freeze/unfreeze timestamps on cards that end CLOSED, or exclude them from the comparison.

issues.summary: The Green account's refund appears as a transaction with status "pending". doc_025 requirement 4 forbids closing a card with any pending transaction and has no bypass. Requirement 5 allows closing with a pending refund after written acknowledgment. The gold uses requirement 5.
evidence: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025: "4. No pending transactions: The card must not have any pending or processing transactions. If pending transactions exist, inform the customer they must wait for all transactions to settle"
doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025: "5. No pending refunds: ... or acknowledge in writing that the refunds will be credited to the linked checking account instead."
db (task agent_data) btxn_d0b8b00ed468: account chk_cr89a2b3c4_3, "REFUND - AMAZON.COM RETURN", amount 89.99, type "refund", status "pending"
gold[19] close dbc_cr89a2b3c4_green; gold[24] order chk_cr89a2b3c4_3 STANDARD/CLASSIC
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that applies requirement 4 literally refuses to close the Green card and orders no replacement, so debit_cards and debit_card_orders differ from the gold. The refund-specific clause is the more natural reading, and the customer script supplies the acknowledgment, so the risk is small.
issues.suggested_fix: Say in requirement 4 that pending refunds are governed by requirement 5, or give the refund row a non-"pending" status such as "refund_pending".

solution_check: Reconstructed: Evergreen is PREMIUM (RUSH $35, PREMIUM design $0), Light Blue is ENTRY with two lost-replacements in 12 months (04/05/2025, 08/10/2025), so the customer accepts the $25 fee but the 48-hour post-closure wait still blocks an order today; Green is MID with a pending refund the customer acknowledges in writing, so close and order STANDARD/CLASSIC. All three cards close with reason stolen. Matches the gold, which replays without errors.
prior_note: Prior review rated this clean; the gold only gained the accounts read in v1.0.1, and neither the freeze-path sensitivity nor the pending-refund overlap was reported before.
notes: Grading-model check against the snapshot: confirmed call_discoverable_agent_tool parses JSON with parse_int=float; reads are logged only when in the gold allowlist; agent_discoverable_tools rows are keyed by tool name only (generate_agent_discoverable_tool_id), so repeat calls collapse to one row; user tools write to the same DB the agent hash covers. Verified scorer (working-repo _verified_db_match) strips closure_reason, but order_debit_card_5739 copies the closed card's closure_reason into the new card's issue_reason (lost/stolen kept, fraud_suspected->fraud, anything else->first_card), so the close reason still decides debit_cards whenever a replacement is ordered after the close. Reason "stolen" matters even under the verified scorer: it becomes issue_reason "stolen" on both new cards. Ordering a replacement before closing (allowed while the old card is FROZEN) yields issue_reason first_card; noted, not counted.
